newsitem.title: UK: Boots down after hayfever drug withdrawal.
newsitem.headline: Boots down after hayfever drug withdrawal.

text.p: Shares in Boots Co Plc were among the biggest decliners in a weak London market on Friday as one of its own-brand hayfever treatments was included in products withdrawn from over-the-counter sales, dealers said.

"It is a bit bearish for the stock," said one dealer. Boots shares, which in recent sessions traded close to their record 708-3/8 set on February 18, were down 6-1/2p or 0.9 percent at 690 by 0806 GMT.
However, analyst William Cullum at Paribas Capital Markets said the news should have "no more than a minor sentiment impact" on Boots shares.

"If you were being ultra cautious you might say that Boots has built a brand name on the basis of reliability and this could damage that brand name, but I think that could be extrapolating too much," Cullum said.
The Paribas analyst added that legal action against the company was unlikely since the drug would have had to pass stringent safety tests before being put on sale.
The Health Department said yesterday that 14 people had died since 1982 from taking the drug terfenadine, included in many hayfever remedies, including one of those sold by Boots.

A spokesman for Boots confirmed that a hayfever product including the drug had been cleared from its shelves and would not be offered for sale, adding that alternative own-label products were available.
